The test image shows a corn stem/stalk with oval tan lesions surrounded by very dark (near-black) borders on what appears to be the leaf sheath. This is a **stem** image. Stem candidates: Anthracnose, Bacterial_Stalk_Rot, Charcoal_Stalk_Rot, Common_Smut, Diplodia_Stalk_Rot, Physoderma_Brown_Spot, Physoderma_Stalk_Rot, Purple_Leaf_Sheath, Stewart_S_Disease.

Top candidates given the dark-bordered tan lesions on leaf sheath: **Physoderma_Brown_Spot**, **Anthracnose_Leaf_Spot_And_Top_Dieback**, **Purple_Leaf_Sheath**.
The Purple_Leaf_Sheath reference is strikingly similar to the test image — oval tan lesions with dark black borders on green leaf sheath. Let me continue checking other classes before confirming.

I've now viewed 16 reference images across 15 different classes. Let me make my assessment.

**Summary of visual comparisons:**

- **Purple_Leaf_Sheath (Corn_Disease_11)**: Near-perfect match — oval tan lesions with very dark black borders on green leaf sheath, same perspective, same lesion distribution pattern as the test image
- **Physoderma_Brown_Spot (stem)**: Dark purple-black smeared spots with reddish discoloration, no tan-centered lesions — not a match
- **Physoderma_Stalk_Rot**: Tiny scattered black dots, no distinct lesions — not a match
- **Anthracnose (stem)**: Internal stalk rot, split open — not a match
- **Charcoal_Stalk_Rot**: Internal shredded stalk tissue — not a match
- **Diplodia_Stalk_Rot**: Dry, collapsed stalk — not a match
- **Bacterial_Stalk_Rot**: Diffuse brown/tan wilting — not a match
- **All leaf diseases (Tar Spot, Gray Leaf Spot, NLB, Eyespot, Common Rust, Goss's Wilt, Holcus Spot)**: Wrong plant part and/or wrong lesion pattern — not matches

The test image shows distinct oval/irregular tan lesions with very prominent dark black borders on a green leaf sheath. This is a textbook match with the **Purple_Leaf_Sheath** reference image (Corn_Disease_11), which shows identical lesion morphology, color, and tissue context.
